verdict.tagline: A fast-paced cooperative challenge plagued by technical friction
for_you_if: you enjoy fast tactical co-op challenges
you have a dedicated group to play with
you can figure out hidden mechanics independently
not_for_you_if: you experience random crashes and poor optimization
you want clear tutorials for character builds
you encounter teammates abandoning matches prematurely

claims.claim: Players experience technical issues including random game crashes, Easy Anti-Cheat errors, and infinite loading screens.

citations.review_text:
I wholeheartedly dissuade anyone from purchasing this game on PC. This is the most unstable game FromSoft has ever put out, and that's saying something.

No amount of reinstallations, reconfigurations, eradication of potentially conflicting software, blood sacrifices to eldritch gods, etc. could prevent this game from crashing at random. There is nothing more crushing than nearing the end of an excellent run and crashing halfway through a boss. 

I hate this game because I want to play it, and it won't let me.
Decent game but dogwater EAC that kept crashing my computer randomly in an interval between 5min-1hour.

Played for multiple attempts across a couple of days and multiple losses. Finally get to the Night Lord and hit an infinite loading screen (which apparently is a known bug) which causes us all to have to quit the game (via task manager) and get no credit for any of that run, which was our first great run.
Disappointing that such a glaring issue can be released in a "game" and be called functional.

claims.claim: The game features a faster-paced, time-dependent structure where players rush across a mostly static map to fight bosses before a timer runs out.

citations.review_text:
Fromsoft design are either awesome great game or just straight up  ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ bad.

I love this game but the fact they only add like 10-20 new type enemy and decided to sale it as whole game .
This game is great the combat is far more fluid but you don't grt anything new if you already have the previous game.
Most of the world were poorly designed simply because the game run on time to get you at one point as fast as possible this is why they skip tons of detail .

It's a disgrace to even had elden ring name in it .

Nightreign was a good time, though it has to be said that as both a multiplayer-focused game and a FromSoftware game it's almost disappointing. There's a fun game in here, especially if you have 2 friends to roll with (I didn't even bother trying to play with randoms), but it does somewhat feel like this was a very fast project meant to cash in on the IP. There's more jank than usual, and the bosses don't all feel like they were designed to fight more than one person at a time. Fighting common enemies is a trivial waste of time, and the game quickly devolves into a sprint around the mostly static map to crush as many bosses as possible before the time is up. There's some solid entertainment here, but it can't be helped that this feels like one of the most "had potential" games ever. I think a [b]3 out of 5[/b] is fair; it's acceptable due to the quality of the gameplay, but just barely. FromSoft are masters of asset re-use, it just usually feels better than this. I'd wait for a sale.

Really cool multiplayer soulsborne game. If you like the genre this will definitely be one that you'll enjoy and  overall a really polished game. Compared to other soulsbornes it is a bit different and more fast paced/time dependent but all in all a big favourite for me and my friends.

This SHOULD be a positive review considering the following: If you like Elden Ring but want it in a more bite-sized and replayable form, this is exactly that. Very fun, approximately 1 hour runs, lots of diversity when using multiple different characters. It's just fun! I really enjoyed playing it.

The bad: For some reason after the 40ish hour mark, the game just suddenly decided it wouldn't work anymore. I could load into the Roundtable Hold and queue for a match, then as soon as I finish queueing the game crashes instantly. That's how it started anyway, now it just crashes on start-up. After attempts to update my drivers, optimize the gameplay settings, etc. I looked up any fixes and it turns out this is a rampant issue that I need to hunt down a solution to with the Admin console in my own pc to resolve some sort of conflict with Windows. While that's fine and dandy for some tech gurus, or even barely novice technology afficianados, I'm too stubborn or too stupid (probably both) to bother with hunting down a fix for a game that should work (and it did for over 40 hours!) when I open it so long as my PC has the appropriate specs.

I am leaving this negative review because FromSoftware and Bandai Namco have completely abandoned Elden Ring Nightreign.

This game has a brilliant cooperative and roguelite foundation, but it severely lacks variety. We are feeling completely left behind. We supported this project from day one, and instead of giving it the long-term content and updates it deserves, the developers dropped a couple of minor patches and walked away to focus on other franchises.

Just because FromSoftware has achieved massive success with Dark Souls and the main Elden Ring game doesn't mean they can treat players of their spin-offs as secondary customers. This absolute lack of post-launch support heavily damages the studio's prestige and reputation.

We DO NOT WANT this game to die. We demand substantial content updates, more boss variety, classes, or whatever. Until FromSoftware shows they care about this community and adds real content, this review will remain negative.

(To everyone reading this: if you feel as abandoned as we do, do not stay silent. Leave your own negative review, spread the word, and vote this up. The only way to pressure FromSoftware and Bandai Namco into listening is by hitting their score. Join the protest and make our voices heard <3)

claims.claim: Players experience matches being ruined by teammates disconnecting or abandoning games prematurely, compounded by penalties for remaining players who leave.

citations.review_text:
Despite all the skepticism at the announcement, I'm glad I was proven wrong about this project.

It's a new Soul's experience, but within the confines of a Battle Royale, it turns out to be a good and engaging thing.
A tandem I had little expectation of, and even less ability to play.
There are a lot of borrowings, a lot of nostalgia, which is deliberately played on.
But it's still wonderful...

My main gripe with this game is players leaving matches for reasons (often as petty as their sense of dignity) or for no reason.
For some, dying to a simple mob on the first day is apparently a real tragedy, and therefore they may run away. It's a shame there's no serious punishment for this; otherwise, perhaps they would have overcome the difficulties, which is exactly what FromSoftware games demand of you.

And finally, I can't ignore the Ⓜ️usic in this game!
Huge respect and thanks to the composers for these new musical masterpieces!

Good game, terrible community. The devs actively punish the player who is stuck in a match where their teammates DC because YOU will get a DC penalty if you leave a match despite being the ONLY person in it. If you get the game, just find a group of friends or a Discord group and then play the game together or just mod it so you can play offline without having to deal with matchmaking and the many, many lost matches due to players who leave, grief, cheat, or more.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that players who leave matches prematurely penalize their remaining teammates' points.

citations.review_text: Probably the worst fromsoft game released. Only thing left to do is reach deep of the night lvl 5 but people leave too often to make it seem possible. You either follow your team or they leave. Run off past the closest boss, die, leave is a solid 80% of the game. The dlc made it even worse with a terrible map design it'll force you to play at times and what feels like the same rotation of bosses. If your teammate leaves, you either wait for a deduction in points or leave and get a higher deduction. The player base has by far one of the worst communities available. 0 communication makes it worse. If you enjoy the game as it is I highly recommend avoiding the dlc since there's no base game deep of the night otherwise. The characters are cool but the map is awful and being forced into it by trying to progress the only thing left to do gets annoying. If you run off and die that is on you, not the team you ran away from.

The Deep of Night mode is such a joke. You have to complete a run to get points to rank up but the entire time you have to pray that you don't end up with a team that will either constantly die or rage quit and make the run literally impossible and pointless. 

The game Expects you to keep playing the THREE player game and waste 30 minutes to an hour of your life just to end up losing because you're missing your other players, but the moment you leave to requeue, the game punishes you for it. Then the game rubs salt in your wound by acknowledging your team raged quit but still punishes you for it. It doesn't matter if they take less points away from you for it because it becomes an uneven number and you end up needing to play an extra game or two or three especially if you're in the higher ranks and the punishment becomes too much and you can't recover. I've went from being almost rank 4 to permanently stuck at rank 2 or freshly 3 because the game punishes me for something that's not my fault.

Its about time we stop defending bad game design just because its a "Souls like game" or people only knowing how to say "Git Gud" or "Skill issue". For too long these games get away from just doing random things that either don't make sense or shouldn't even happen just because the developers say its to make the games harder. It doesn't make the game more challenging it makes it more annoying.

It's okay if you don't play well, but if you just quit the game because of a mistake and cause your teammates to lose points for no reason, then show your profile so others can insult you. Stop fooling yourself like a baby who never grew up in their mom's arms. You're spineless, you're nothing, ♥♥♥♥ you.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the game as lacking a tutorial or clear explanations for character builds, items, and passive effects.

citations.review_text:
TLDR: Great game. Love it to death. Ignore the review and play it if you're looking for a good time. Read on if you care about the current state of multiplayer in FromSoft titles (and are a fellow masochist).

I forgot to review this game back when I was actually playing it. To remedy this tragedy, here is a reality check:

Nightreign is the poster child of lost opportunity, the ultimate example of what could have been. As a friend put it, a bastion of lost potential.

I am not talking about what some complain to be the lack of content in a game teeming with reused assets. 

I am not complaining about the lack of true PoI and boss randomisation in what is a roguelike spinoff. 

I am not even complaining about the gameplay balance or the misleading, opaque descriptions of items, passive effects and abilities.

No, all those pale in comparison to the most barebones implementation of multiplayer functionality in any game I've ever seen, such as:

- No crossplay
- No regional matchmaking 
- No ping limits
- No or too few measures targetting cheaters, hackers and griefers
- No proper communication system beyond simple pings
- No dedicated lobbies with matchmaking filters, such as for expedition time, dlc ownership, etc.

This isn't anything new. Some of these were common complaints from the network test. What's baffling is that, one year later, they have not been addressed. With the most recent patch being more than six months ago, I am not convinced they ever will be.

For a game whose entire shtick is coop, this spells doom for its future. There is no longevity baked into what is otherwise a fantastic game. There is no clarification of the support timeline post-dlc release. There is no apparent improvement to the legacy net code that haunts the mind and spirit of every souls player, with its game-breaking desync's and jarring packet loss. To top it off, complete radio silence from FromSoft that they even recognise these longstanding issues raised by the player base, in…

I’ve put a lot of hours into Elden Ring Nightreign, mostly playing with the same group of friends over the past year. Most of them were completely new to Soulslike games, while I was already familiar with FromSoftware’s style, and somehow the game managed to work equally well for all of us.

Nightreign is surprisingly grounded and restrained. It isn’t constantly throwing flashy rewards or endless explanations at you, and that is part of what makes it so satisfying. Every character supports a variety of builds and playstyles, but in classic FromSoftware fashion, the game barely explains any of them. You have to experiment, explore and gradually figure out what works.

Once you learn the basics, the game becomes incredibly addictive. The moment-to-moment gameplay is consistently fun, whether you are underpowered at the beginning of a run, fully equipped near the end, playing alone or fighting alongside friends. There is a particular kind of magic to its gameplay loop that keeps pulling you back for another run.

Between the bosses, enemies, weapons, character builds and small hidden mechanics, there is always something new to discover or master. Even after playing for so long, it still feels like there is never enough time to explore everything the game has to offer.

It does sometimes feel as though the developers have forgotten about the game, but the community collectively shares the delusion that new content will arrive one day. Until then, community mods have been a blessing. Some of them add so much high-quality content that you occasionally forget you are playing fan-made additions rather than official updates.

Anyone who has played another FromSoftware game will immediately feel at home. Nightreign builds on knowledge you already have from games such as Elden Ring, but reshapes those familiar mechanics to fit a completely different structure. As someone who also played Elden Ring with the Seamless Co-op mod, Nightreign feels very different during ex…
